senses.definition: a mark, sign, or line left by something that has moved or existed there
senses.definitionCN: 某物经过或存在后留下的记号、迹象或线条
senses.example: There were fresh traces in the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 雪地上有新鲜的痕迹。
senses.why: Latin trahere meant to draw or pull. A trace is what a moving thing draws across a surface, so the mark is literally a line pulled behind it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 trahere 意为“拉、拖”。trace 就是移动之物在表面上拖出的东西，因此痕迹字面上就是它身后被拉出的线。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.titleCN: 微量：只剩一点点痕迹
senses.definition: a very small amount of a substance or quality, barely enough to be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 极少量的物质或性质，仅够被察觉
senses.example: The water contained traces of lead.
senses.exampleCN: 水中含有微量铅。
senses.why: When almost everything has gone, what remains is a mark of what was there. The tiny residue is treated as the trace of the vanished whole.
senses.whyCN: 当几乎所有东西都消失，剩下的就是“它曾在此”的记号。极小的残余被当作消失整体的痕迹。

senses.title: To follow the marks
senses.titleCN: 追踪：顺着脚印走
senses.definition: to follow the marks or signs left by a person, animal, or thing in order to find it
senses.definitionCN: 沿着人或动物、物体留下的痕迹走，以找到它
senses.example: The dog traced the scent through the woods.
senses.exampleCN: 狗循着气味穿过树林追踪。
senses.why: If a trace is a line pulled behind a moving thing, following that line reverses the movement. The verb is the mark read backwards.
senses.whyCN: 如果 trace 是移动之物身后拖出的线，那么顺着线走就是反向还原那次移动。动词就是倒着读那道痕迹。

senses.title: To trace an origin
senses.titleCN: 追溯：沿着线索回到源头
senses.definition: to find the origin or cause of something by following evidence
senses.definitionCN: 沿着证据找到某物的起源或原因
senses.example: Historians traced the custom back to the 12th century.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把这个习俗追溯到 12 世纪。
senses.why: The line does not have to be physical. A record is a trace in paper, and following it backwards leads to the source rather than to a place.
senses.whyCN: 这条线不必是实物。记录就是纸上的痕迹，倒着顺它走，到达的是源头而不是地点。

senses.title: To copy an outline
senses.titleCN: 描摹：把底下的线透出来
senses.definition: to copy a drawing or design by following its lines, often through thin paper
senses.definitionCN: 沿着线条复制图画或图案，常透过薄纸进行
senses.example: She traced the pattern onto the fabric.
senses.exampleCN: 她把图案描摹到布料上。
senses.why: Here the hand draws a line that already exists below. The trace is both the original line and the new one, so copying and marking meet.
senses.whyCN: 这里手画的是一条本来就在下面的线。痕迹既是被描的原线，也是新画的线，复制与留痕在此相遇。

senses.title: To draw a course or outline
senses.titleCN: 勾勒：把路线画成一条线
senses.definition: to draw or mark out a route, boundary, or shape
senses.definitionCN: 画出或标出路线、边界或形状
senses.example: He traced the river's course on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 他在地图上勾勒出这条河的走向。
senses.why: A drawn route is a trace made in advance rather than left behind. The same pulling gesture now points forward, mapping what will be followed.
senses.whyCN: 画出的路线是提前留下的痕迹，而不是事后留下的。同一个“拉线”动作现在指向前方，标出将被遵循的路。

senses.title: The record made by an instrument
senses.titleCN: 轨迹：仪器画出的那条线
senses.definition: a line or curve recorded by an instrument such as a seismograph or heart monitor
senses.definitionCN: 地震仪或心脏监护仪等仪器记录下的线或曲线
senses.example: The trace showed a small tremor at 3 a.m.
senses.exampleCN: 记录曲线显示凌晨三点有一次轻微震动。
senses.why: A machine draws what it detects, producing the same kind of line a walking body leaves. The paper trace is a mark made by movement it never saw.
senses.whyCN: 机器把它检测到的东西画成线，产生与行走身体留下的同类线条。纸上的轨迹，是它从未看见的移动所留下的记号。

senses.title: A harness strap (plural)
senses.titleCN: 挽具绳：把力拉向前的带子
senses.definition: one of the straps by which a vehicle or plough is drawn by an animal, usually in the plural traces
senses.definitionCN: 役畜拉动车辆或犁时所用的皮带之一，通常用复数 traces
senses.example: The horse pulled against the traces.
senses.exampleCN: 马用力拉紧挽绳。
senses.why: This sense keeps the literal trahere: the straps are what pull. The same root that gives a drawn line gives the leather that draws a plough.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了字面的 trahere“拉”：挽绳就是用来拉的东西。给出“画线”的同一词根，也给出了拉犁的皮带。

intro.en: Trace comes from Latin trahere 'to draw, pull', through its noun tractus 'a drawing, course', and Old French tracier 'to follow a track'. The mark and the act of following grew from one root.
intro.cn: trace 来自拉丁语 trahere“拉、拖”，经其名词 tractus“拉出的线、行程”，再经古法语 tracier“循迹而行”。痕迹与追踪这两个义项，从同一个词根长出。

items.en: Trahere meant to draw, drag, or pull. It is the root of a large family: tractor, attract, contract, extract, subtract.
items.cn: trahere 意为拉、拖、牵引。它是一大家族的词根：tractor、attract、contract、extract、subtract。

items.en: Tractus was a drawing, a dragging, a course, or a stretch of land. The 'course' sense is the bridge to a line left on the ground.
items.cn: tractus 意为拉、拖、行程，也指一片延伸的土地。“行程”义是从“拉”走向“地面上的线”的桥梁。

items.en: Tracier meant to follow a track or to make a mark. Old French also had trace, a track or footprint.
items.cn: tracier 意为循迹而行或留下记号。古法语还有名词 trace，指足迹或踪迹。

items.en: English took trace in the 14c. for a track or footprint, and the verb for following one. The copying sense appears later.
items.cn: 英语 14 世纪借入 trace，指足迹或踪迹，动词指循迹而行。“描摹”义出现得更晚。

items.en: Scientific instruments gave the word its recorded-line sense: a seismograph or barograph leaves a trace on paper.
items.cn: 科学仪器赋予这个词“记录线”义：地震仪或气压计在纸上留下 trace。

items.en: The chemical 'trace amount' sense grew in the 19c. with analytical chemistry, and computing added trace logs and stack traces.
items.cn: 化学上的“微量”义随 19 世纪分析化学发展，计算机又增加了 trace 日志与堆栈跟踪。

note.en: The first group is the trace family and its derivatives; the second separates marks, paths, and tiny amounts.
note.cn: 第一组是 trace 词族及其派生词；第二组区分“痕迹、路径、微量”三类近义词。

entries.definition: able to be followed or traced to a source.
entries.definitionCN: 可追踪的；可追溯到源头的。

entries.definition: a person or instrument that tracks, or a substance used to follow a process.
entries.definitionCN: 追踪者或追踪仪器；示踪剂。

entries.definition: the ornamental stone lines in a Gothic window. It is lines for their own sake.
entries.definitionCN: 哥特式窗户中的装饰性石线；窗花格。它是为线条而线条。

entries.definition: to go back over a route or to reconstruct a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 重走某条路线；重新梳理某个过程。

entries.definition: a series of marks or a path made by repeated movement. It is a trace made by many feet, not one.
entries.definitionCN: 一连串记号或反复行走形成的路径。它是许多脚印而非一个留下的 trace。

entries.definition: a mark or smell left by a moving thing, or to follow behind it. It stresses the continuous line left in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 移动之物留下的痕迹或气味，或在其后跟随。它强调运动中留下的连续线。

entries.definition: a small remaining part of something that has almost disappeared. It is the formal word for the 'tiny amount' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎消失之物留下的一小部分。它是“微量”义的正式说法。

entries.definition: a small piece of evidence or a slight amount. It points to what might be true rather than to what passed.
entries.definitionCN: 少量证据或一丝迹象。它指向“可能是什么”，而不是“什么曾经经过”。

entries.definition: the outer line of a shape, or a summary. It matches the drawing senses of trace.
entries.definitionCN: 形状的外沿线，或内容提要。它对应 trace 的描绘义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin trahere 'draw, pull' and tractus 'a drawing, course'. Family words trace, traceable, tracer, tracery, retrace; relatives tractor, attract, extract.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 trahere“拉、拖”与 tractus“拉出的线、行程”。词族为 trace、traceable、tracer、tracery、retrace；亲属词 tractor、attract、extract。

normal.en: Trahere is to pull; a trace is the line a passing thing pulls behind it.
normal.cn: trahere 是拉；trace 就是经过之物在身后拉出的线。

normal.en: A tractor and a trace share the same pulling root.
normal.cn: tractor 与 trace 共享同一个“拉”的词根。

normal.en: To trace a call is to read a paper trail backwards.
normal.cn: trace 一通电话，就是倒着读纸上的痕迹。

normal.en: A trace element is what remains when almost everything is gone.
normal.cn: 微量元素，就是几乎全部消失后剩下的那一点。

normal.en: Traces of a harness are the straps that literally pull the plough.
normal.cn: 挽具的 traces，就是字面上拉着犁的那些皮带。

abstract.en: Nothing passes through the world without drawing a line on it.
abstract.cn: 没有任何东西经过世界而不在上面画下一道线。

abstract.en: To trace is to trust that the line still points to what made it.
abstract.cn: 追溯，就是相信那道线仍然指向留下它的东西。

abstract.en: We are known less by what we leave than by who can read it.
abstract.cn: 我们之被认识，与其说靠留下什么，不如说靠谁能读懂它。

examples.en: The isotope leaves a trace in the rock that can be measured.
examples.cn: 这种同位素在岩石中留下可测量的痕迹。

examples.en: She traced her family back to a fishing village in the north.
examples.cn: 她把家族渊源追溯到北方一个渔村。

examples.en: The child traced the letters with a finger.
examples.cn: 孩子用手指描摹那些字母。

dict_mnemonic.text: “追死”——顺着脚印追到死胡同也要追 → trace 追踪、痕迹

root: 源自拉丁语 trahere“拉、拖”，经名词 tractus“拉出的线、行程”与古法语 tracier“循迹而行”进入英语；核心是“拖出来的一条线”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of trace, all one line: something moving draws a line, and that line can be a footprint, a tiny residue, a followed path, an origin, a copied outline, a drawn route, an instrument record, or a pulling strap.
sensesIntro.cn: trace 的八个义项都是同一条线：移动之物拉出一道线，这道线可以是脚印、微量残余、被追随的路径、源头、描摹的轮廓、画出的路线、仪器记录，或拉车的皮带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faint line of footprints leading away across wet ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿地上延伸远去的一行浅浅脚印。

chain: OLD FRENCH TRACIER = FOLLOW A TRACK

branches.en: MARK AND RESIDUE: a full mark and the last faint remainder are the same line at different strengths.
branches.cn: 痕迹与残余：完整的痕迹与最后一点淡淡残余，是同一条线在不同强度下。

branches.en: FOLLOWING: the marks lead either to a place or backwards to a source.
branches.cn: 追随：痕迹或把人引到某个地点，或反向引到某个源头。

branches.en: DRAWING: the line can be copied from below or laid down in advance as a route.
branches.cn: 描绘：线可以从下面被描下来，也可以预先画成一条路线。

branches.en: RECORD: an instrument draws the line on paper without ever seeing what moved.
branches.cn: 记录：仪器在纸上画出线，却从未看见是什么在移动。

branches.en: PULLING: the harness traces keep the oldest literal sense of trahere, leather that draws a load.
branches.cn: 牵引：挽具 traces 保留了 trahere 最古老的字面义——拉重物的皮带。

intro.en: Trace's family is built on Latin trahere. English adds -able, -er, -ery, and re-, and uses fixed phrases for the tiny-amount sense.
intro.cn: trace 的词族建立在拉丁语 trahere 上。英语加 -able、-er、-ery、re-，并用固定短语表达“微量”义。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are trahere 'to draw', tractus 'a drawing or course', and tractare 'to handle, drag about'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 trahere“拉”、tractus“拉出的线、行程”，以及 tractare“反复处理、拖来拖去”。

items.meaning: able to be followed to its source
items.meaningCN: 可追踪的；可追溯的（-able 表示“可被”）
items.example: The infection was traceable to a single supplier.
items.exampleCN: 这次感染可以追溯到单一供应商。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to be traced
items.meaningCN: 可追溯性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: Food traceability rules now cover every batch.
items.exampleCN: 食品可追溯规定现在覆盖每一批货。

items.meaning: one that tracks, or a substance used to follow a process
items.meaningCN: 追踪者；示踪剂（-er 表示执行者）
items.example: Radioactive tracers showed how the fluid moved.
items.exampleCN: 放射性示踪剂显示了流体的运动方式。

items.meaning: ornamental intersecting lines, especially in Gothic windows
items.meaningCN: 窗花格；装饰性交错线条（-ery 构成集合或装饰名词）
items.example: The rose window is filled with stone tracery.
items.exampleCN: 玫瑰窗布满石制窗花格。

items.meaning: to go back over a route or reconstruct a sequence
items.meaningCN: 重走；回溯（re- 表示再次、返回）
items.example: We retraced our steps to the fork in the path.
items.exampleCN: 我们沿原路返回到岔路口。

items.meaning: to follow evidence to an earlier origin
items.meaningCN: 追溯；往回追查（back 表示方向）
items.example: The rumour can be traced back to one blog post.
items.exampleCN: 这个传言可以追溯到一篇博客文章。

items.meaning: to mark or draw a plan or boundary
items.meaningCN: 画出；标出（out 表示使显现）
items.example: They traced out the new border on the ground.
items.exampleCN: 他们在地上标出了新边界。

items.meaning: to draw over existing lines, often to copy them
items.meaningCN: 描过；沿着原线描画
items.example: She traced over the pencil sketch in ink.
items.exampleCN: 她用墨水描过铅笔草图。

items.meaning: leaving no sign at all
items.meaningCN: 无影无踪；没留下任何痕迹
items.example: The boat vanished without a trace.
items.exampleCN: 那艘船消失得无影无踪。

items.meaning: a chemical element present in extremely small amounts
items.meaningCN: 微量元素；含量极少的化学元素
items.example: Zinc is a trace element essential to the body.
items.exampleCN: 锌是人体必需的微量元素。

latinEntries.structure: past participle and noun of trahere
latinEntries.meaning: drawn; a drawing, course, or stretch
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被拉出的；拉、行程、延伸的一片

latinEntries.meaning: to handle, work at, drag about
latinEntries.meaningCN: 反复处理；操作；拖来拖去

definition_en: a custom or belief passed down from earlier generations, the act of handing something down, or an established artistic or religious body of practice
core_image: 一只手把一件东西递到另一只手里，一代接一代不停。
scene: The village still keeps the tradition of baking bread on the first day of spring.
sceneCN: 这里 tradition 是「传统做法」（第 1 个义项：世代传下的习俗）；句意：这个村庄仍保留着立春第一天烤面包的传统。场景要点：土炉、面包、围裙、春日的田野。

senses.title: A custom passed down
senses.titleCN: 传统：一代递到一代的习俗
senses.definition: a custom, practice, or way of doing something passed from earlier generations to later ones
senses.definitionCN: 从先辈传给后代的习俗、做法或行事方式
senses.example: It is a tradition to light candles on the graves.
senses.exampleCN: 在墓前点蜡烛是一项传统。
senses.why: Latin tradere is to hand over. A tradition is the object that has been handed from hand to hand so many times that no one remembers the first owner.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tradere 是“递交、交出”。传统就是一件被一只手递到另一只手、递了太多次的东西，以至没人记得最初的主人。

senses.title: A body of inherited beliefs
senses.titleCN: 传统观念：整套传下来的信念
senses.definition: the accumulated beliefs, values, and assumptions of a community, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体累积下来的信念、价值与预设的整体
senses.example: The novel challenges the tradition of the obedient daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说挑战了“顺从女儿”的传统观念。
senses.why: Many handed-over objects form a warehouse. When the word names all of them together, tradition means the inherited belief system rather than one custom.
senses.whyCN: 许多被递交的东西聚成一座仓库。当这个词把它们整体命名，tradition 就指承袭下来的信念体系，而不是单项习俗。

senses.title: The act of handing down
senses.titleCN: 传承：递交这个动作本身
senses.definition: the process of passing knowledge, customs, or stories from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 把知识、习俗或故事从一代传到下一代的过程
senses.example: The tradition of the craft depends on apprentices working beside masters.
senses.exampleCN: 这门手艺的传承依靠学徒在师傅身边工作。
senses.why: Here the emphasis falls on the verb hidden in the noun: the handover itself. Tradition is not the thing but the passing, and it can fail if no one takes it.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调的是名词里隐藏的动词：递交本身。tradition 不是那件东西，而是传递过程；若无人接住，它就会中断。

senses.title: An artistic or literary lineage
senses.titleCN: 流派：艺术上的一支传递链
senses.definition: an established body of artistic, literary, or musical practice inherited from earlier works or artists
senses.definitionCN: 从早期作品或艺术家继承下来的成体系的、文学的或音乐的实践
senses.example: He writes within the tradition of the American short story.
senses.exampleCN: 他在美国短篇小说的传统里写作。
senses.why: Works are handed down too. A line of writers passing forms to one another becomes a tradition, and a new work can join it or refuse it.
senses.whyCN: 作品也会被递交。一列作家把形式传给彼此，就成了传统；新作品可以加入它，也可以拒绝它。

senses.title: Religious tradition
senses.titleCN: 圣传：信仰共同体递交的教导
senses.definition: the body of teaching and practice handed down within a religious community, especially beyond written scripture
senses.definitionCN: 宗教共同体内部传下的教导与实践，尤指经文之外的部分
senses.example: The church defends its tradition alongside its scriptures.
senses.exampleCN: 教会在经文之外也维护自己的圣传。
senses.why: For a community that believes its teaching was delivered to it, tradition is almost a legal term: the deposit handed over once and kept intact.
senses.whyCN: 对于一个相信教导是“交付给它”的共同体，tradition 几乎是个法律词：一次交托、完整保存的遗产。

senses.title: Habitual practice
senses.titleCN: 惯例：年年都这么办
senses.definition: an established habit or usual way of doing things, often without deep historical weight
senses.definitionCN: 既定的习惯或通常做法，未必有很深的历史分量
senses.example: By tradition, the youngest member speaks first.
senses.exampleCN: 按照惯例，最年轻的成员先发言。
senses.why: The handover can be shallow: one generation simply copies the last. When the chain is short and unreflective, tradition means convention rather than heritage.
senses.whyCN: 递交可以是浅的：一代只是照抄上一代。当链条短而不加反思，tradition 就是惯例，而不是厚重遗产。

senses.title: A story handed down (older use)
senses.titleCN: 传说：口头递交的故事
senses.definition: an older sense: a story or account handed down orally, often without verification
senses.definitionCN: 较古的义项：口头传下、常未经核实的故事或说法
senses.example: According to tradition, the well was dug by a saint.
senses.exampleCN: 据传说，这口井是一位圣徒挖的。
senses.why: Oral handing is the oldest channel. A story that travels by mouth for centuries becomes a tradition, and the word can name the story itself.
senses.whyCN: 口头递交是最古老的渠道。一个靠嘴流传数百年的故事就成了 tradition，这个词也可以直接指那个故事。

senses.title: Legal delivery (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 交付：法律上的“递到手中”
senses.definition: the archaic legal sense of delivery or surrender of property into another's possession
senses.definitionCN: 较古的法律义：把财产交付或让渡给他人占有
senses.example: The deed records the tradition of the land to the heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据记录了土地向继承人的交付。
senses.why: This is traditio in its strictest Roman-law sense: actual handing over. Every other sense is a metaphor built on this physical delivery.
senses.whyCN: 这是 traditio 最严格的罗马法意义：实际的递交。其他所有义项，都是建立在这个物理交付上的比喻。

intro.en: Tradition comes from Latin traditio 'a handing over', from tradere 'to hand over', itself trans- 'across' plus dare 'to give'. The word begins as a legal delivery and ends as inherited custom.
intro.cn: tradition 来自拉丁语 traditio“递交”，来自 tradere“交出”，后者是 trans-“越过”加 dare“给”。这个词从法律上的交付，走到承袭的习俗。

items.en: Dare meant to give. It is one of the most productive verbs in Latin, behind data, date, edit, and tradition.
items.cn: dare 意为“给”。它是拉丁语中构词能力最强的动词之一，支撑着 data、date、edit 与 tradition。

items.en: Trans- meant across. Transdare, later tradere, meant to give across, that is, to hand something over to another.
items.cn: trans- 意为“越过”。transdare（后作 tradere）意为“越过地给”，即把东西交到别人手里。

items.en: Traditio was the noun of action: a delivery, surrender, or transmission. Roman law used it for the actual transfer of possession.
items.cn: traditio 是动作名词：交付、让渡、传递。罗马法用它指实际移转占有。

items.en: Old French tradition carried both the legal and the religious senses. The church's teaching was thought of as delivered once and kept.
items.cn: 古法语 tradition 同时承载法律义与宗教义。教会的教导被视为一次交付、此后保存。

items.en: English adopted tradition in the 14c. for the transmission of doctrine and custom. By the 16c. it commonly meant an inherited way of doing things.
items.cn: 英语 14 世纪借入 tradition，指教义与习俗的传递。到 16 世纪，它常指承袭下来的行事方式。

items.en: The modern word covers custom, communal belief, artistic lineage, and oral story. The legal sense survives only in specialist writing.
items.cn: 现代词覆盖习俗、群体信念、艺术流派与口头故事。法律义只残留在专业文献中。

note.en: The first group is tradition's own family; the second separates custom, habit, heritage, and legend by what is actually handed down.
note.cn: 第一组是 tradition 自身的词族；第二组按“究竟递交了什么”区分习俗、习惯、遗产与传说。

entries.definition: following or belonging to an established tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循或属于既定传统的。

entries.definition: in the way that has long been established.
entries.definitionCN: 按照长期沿袭的方式；传统上。

entries.definition: the belief that traditional practices should be preserved.
entries.definitionCN: 认为传统做法应予保存的信念；传统主义。

entries.definition: a person who defends traditional beliefs or methods.
entries.definitionCN: 维护传统信念或方法的人；传统主义者。

entries.definition: a particular way of behaving that a group has followed for a long time. It is usually local and specific.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体长期遵循的特定行为方式。它通常是地方性的、具体的。

entries.definition: a usual and accepted way of doing something, often by tacit agreement. It needs less history than tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 通常且被接受的做法，常出于默契。它需要的历时尚短于 tradition。

entries.definition: valued things, buildings, or culture inherited from the past. It stresses what is owned and preserved, not the act of passing.
entries.definitionCN: 从过去继承的珍贵事物、建筑或文化。它强调被拥有与保存的东西，而非传递动作。

entries.definition: a habitual way of doing something. It is neutral and can be new, unlike tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性的做法。它中性，也可以是新的，与 tradition 不同。

entries.definition: an old story, often unverifiable. It matches the oral-story sense of tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 古老的、常无法核实的故事。它对应 tradition 的口头故事义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin trans- 'across' + dare 'give' gives tradere 'hand over', and traditio 'a delivery'. Family words tradition, traditional, traditionalism, traditionalist.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 trans-“越过”+ dare“给”构成 tradere“递交”，再构成 traditio“交付”。词族为 tradition、traditional、traditionalism、traditionalist。

normal.en: Tradition is trans + dare: giving something across the generations.
normal.cn: tradition 就是 trans + dare：把东西越过代际递给别人。

normal.en: The legal traditio is a literal handover; every other sense is that handover repeated.
normal.cn: 法律上的 traditio 是字面的递交；其他义项都是这次递交的重复。

normal.en: An oral tradition is a story carried by mouths instead of hands.
normal.cn: 口传传统，是靠嘴而不是靠手携带的故事。

normal.en: Break with tradition is to refuse to take what is being handed to you.
normal.cn: break with tradition，就是拒绝接住递过来的东西。

normal.en: Traditionalist and traditionalism both guard the chain of hands.
normal.cn: traditionalist 与 traditionalism，都在守护那条由手连成的链。

abstract.en: Tradition is a gift that only survives if someone accepts it.
abstract.cn: 传统是一份礼物，只有有人接受才活得下去。

abstract.en: We inherit the shape of our questions before we learn to ask them.
abstract.cn: 我们先继承问题的形状，然后才学会提问。

abstract.en: A tradition is not the past; it is the past still being handed over now.
abstract.cn: 传统不是过去，而是此刻仍在被递交的过去。

examples.en: The tradition of reading aloud survived longer than the printing press.
examples.cn: 朗读的传统比印刷术延续得更久。

examples.en: She broke with tradition and asked her father to walk her to the ceremony.
examples.cn: 她打破传统，请父亲陪她走到仪式现场。

examples.en: According to tradition, the first settlers arrived during a drought.
examples.cn: 据传说，最早定居者是在一次旱灾期间到达的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “传地神”——把土地神像一代代递下去 → tradition 传统、传承

root: 源自拉丁语 tradere“递交、交出”（trans-“越过”+ dare“给”），名词 traditio“交付”；核心是“一代递到下一代”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tradition, all one handover: a custom, a belief system, the act of passing, an artistic lineage, a religious deposit, a habit, an oral story, or a legal delivery of property.
sensesIntro.cn: tradition 的八个义项都是一次递交：习俗、信念体系、传递动作、艺术流派、宗教遗产、惯例、口头故事，或法律上的财产交付。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand passing an object into another hand, over and over.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件递到另一只手里，一次又一次。

branches.en: CUSTOM: a deep inherited practice and a shallow habitual one are the same handover at different depths.
branches.cn: 习俗：深厚的承袭做法与浅层的习惯做法，是同一次递交在不同深度上。

branches.en: BELIEF: a community's whole warehouse of assumptions, and a church's guarded deposit, are handed-down bodies of teaching.
branches.cn: 信念：一个群体整套预设的仓库，与教会守护的遗产，都是传下的教导体系。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER ITSELF: the act of passing, from Roman property delivery to the survival of a craft.
branches.cn: 递交本身：从罗马法的财产交付，到一门手艺的延续，都是传递动作。

branches.en: ARTISTIC LINEAGE: forms and styles are handed from one writer or artist to the next.
branches.cn: 艺术流派：形式与风格从一位作者或艺术家传到下一位。

branches.en: ORAL STORY: the oldest channel is the mouth, and the story itself can take the name of the tradition.
branches.cn: 口头故事：最古老的渠道是嘴，故事本身也可以承担 tradition 这个名字。

intro.en: Tradition's family is built on Latin tradere. English adds -al, -ally, -ism, and -ist, and negates with un-; phrases carry the legal and oral senses.
intro.cn: tradition 的词族建立在拉丁语 tradere 上。英语加 -al、-ally、-ism、-ist，并用 un- 否定；短语承载法律义与口传义。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are dare 'to give', tradere 'to hand over', and traditio 'a delivery or transmission'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 dare“给”、tradere“递交”，以及 traditio“交付、传递”。

items.meaning: following or belonging to an established tradition
items.meaningCN: 传统的；遵循既定传统的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Traditional bread is baked in a wood oven.
items.exampleCN: 传统面包在木炉里烤制。

items.meaning: in the long-established way
items.meaningCN: 传统上；按长期沿袭的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Traditionally, the harvest begins after the first rain.
items.exampleCN: 传统上，收割在初雨之后开始。

items.meaning: the belief that traditional practices should be preserved
items.meaningCN: 传统主义；主张保存传统做法的信念（-ism 构成主义）
items.example: His traditionalism resisted every reform.
items.exampleCN: 他的传统主义抵制每一项改革。

items.meaning: a person who defends traditional beliefs or methods
items.meaningCN: 传统主义者；维护传统的人（-ist 表示人）
items.example: Traditionalists opposed the new liturgy.
items.exampleCN: 传统主义者反对新的礼拜仪式。

items.meaning: not following established tradition
items.meaningCN: 非传统的；不循惯例的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: They chose an untraditional venue for the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼选了一个非传统的场地。

items.meaning: constrained by tradition
items.meaningCN: 受传统束缚的（bound 表示被捆绑）
items.example: The industry is tradition-bound and slow to change.
items.exampleCN: 这个行业受传统束缚，变革缓慢。

items.meaning: knowledge or stories passed on by speech rather than writing
items.meaningCN: 口传传统；靠口头而非文字传递的知识或故事
items.example: The epic survived through oral tradition.
items.exampleCN: 这部史诗通过口传传统流传下来。

items.meaning: according to long-established custom
items.meaningCN: 按照传统；按惯例
items.example: By tradition, the eldest son inherits the farm.
items.exampleCN: 按照传统，长子继承农场。

items.meaning: to depart from established custom
items.meaningCN: 打破传统；背离惯例
items.example: The chef broke with tradition and served no pudding.
items.exampleCN: 这位厨师打破传统，没有上布丁。

items.meaning: a long-established practice belonging to a group
items.meaningCN: ……的传统（of 标记所属群体或内容）
items.example: The school has a tradition of public service.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校有公共服务的传统。

definition_zh: 转移；调动；转账；转让；换乘
definition_en: to move something or someone from one place, holder, or vehicle to another, or the act of doing so
core_image: 把一只箱子从一辆车搬到另一辆车上。
scene: She transferred to a slower train at the border.
sceneCN: 这里 transfer 是「换乘」（第 5 个义项：从一种交通工具换到另一种）；句意：她在边境换乘了一列较慢的火车。场景要点：边境站台、两列火车、行李箱、换乘指示牌。

pos.zh: 转移；调动；转账；转让；换乘
转移；调动；转账；换乘；转印图

senses.title: Move something to another place
senses.titleCN: 搬移：把东西挪到别处
senses.definition: to move an object, group, or quantity from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把物体、群体或数量从一处移到另一处
senses.example: The files were transferred to a secure server.
senses.exampleCN: 文件被转移到一台安全服务器上。
senses.why: Latin transferre is trans- 'across' plus ferre 'carry'. The core is a hand carrying a load across a boundary, so any change of location can use the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 transferre 是 trans-“越过”加 ferre“搬运”。核心是一只手把货物搬过一条界线，因此任何位置变化都能用这个词。

senses.title: Move a person to another job or school
senses.titleCN: 调动：把人挪到另一个岗位
senses.definition: to move a person to a different job, department, school, or team
senses.definitionCN: 把某人调到不同的工作、部门、学校或团队
senses.example: He transferred to the Beijing office last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年春天调到了北京办公室。
senses.why: A person is the load now. The boundary crossed is institutional rather than physical, but the carrying motion is the same.
senses.whyCN: 现在“货物”是人。越过的界线是制度性的而非物理的，但搬运的动作相同。

senses.title: Move money between accounts
senses.titleCN: 转账：把钱从一手交到另一手
senses.definition: to send money from one account, person, or country to another
senses.definitionCN: 把钱从一个账户、人或国家转到另一个
senses.example: She transferred the deposit to the landlord's account.
senses.exampleCN: 她把押金转到房东的账户。
senses.why: Money is an abstract load. Transferring it moves the claim, not the paper, but the image of a handover survives in every bank statement.
senses.whyCN: 钱是抽象的货物。转账移动的是请求权而不是纸钞，但“递交”的意象在每份银行流水里都活着。

senses.title: Transfer ownership or rights
senses.titleCN: 转让：把权利交出去
senses.definition: to legally convey ownership, rights, or title from one party to another
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上把所有权、权利或产权从一方移转给另一方
senses.example: The land was transferred to the trust in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地于 1998 年转让给信托机构。
senses.why: This is the oldest legal sense: the actual delivery of property into another's possession. Here the word is almost literal again.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的法律义：实际把财产交付他人占有。这里这个词几乎又回到了字面。

senses.title: Change from one vehicle or route
senses.titleCN: 换乘：把自己从一车搬到另一车
senses.definition: to change from one bus, train, or flight to another in order to continue a journey
senses.definitionCN: 为继续行程而从一辆公交、火车或航班换到另一辆
senses.example: Passengers transfer at the central station.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客在中央车站换乘。
senses.why: The traveller is both the load and the carrier. At the platform, a body crosses from one vehicle to another, which is the core image exactly.
senses.whyCN: 旅客既是货物也是搬运者。在站台上，身体从一辆车跨到另一辆，正是核心意象本身。

senses.title: Shift attention, feeling, or loyalty
senses.titleCN: 转移：注意力与情感的搬家
senses.definition: to direct attention, emotion, or loyalty away from one object and toward another
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力、情感或忠诚从一个对象转向另一个
senses.example: He transferred his affection to the younger son.
senses.exampleCN: 他把感情转移到了小儿子身上。
senses.why: What is carried is not visible: attention or love. The word treats an inner attachment as a load that can be moved from one person to another.
senses.whyCN: 被搬运的东西看不见：注意力或爱。这个词把内心的依恋当作可以从一个人搬到另一个人的货物。

senses.title: A player's move between clubs
senses.titleCN: 转会：球员从一个队搬到另一个队
senses.definition: the movement of a sports player from one club to another, often for a fee
senses.definitionCN: 运动员从一个俱乐部转到另一个，常涉及转会费
senses.example: The transfer broke the league record.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔转会打破了联赛纪录。
senses.why: Sport uses the employment sense at high price. The player is the load, the clubs are the vehicles, and the fee pays for the carrying.
senses.whyCN: 体育把“调动”义标上高价。球员是货物，俱乐部是车辆，转会费就是搬运的代价。

senses.title: Print or copy onto another surface
senses.titleCN: 转印：把图案搬到另一表面
senses.definition: to print, copy, or apply an image or pattern onto a different surface
senses.definitionCN: 把图像或图案印、复制或施加到另一表面
senses.example: The design is transferred onto the ceramic with a decal.
senses.exampleCN: 图案用贴花转印到陶瓷上。
senses.why: The image is carried across from paper to clay. Nothing physical changes hands, but the pattern is moved intact, which is transfer in its cleanest technical form.
senses.whyCN: 图像从纸被搬到陶土上。没有实物易手，但图案完整地被移动，这是 transfer 最干净的技术形态。

intro.en: Transfer is Latin transferre, 'to carry across', built from trans- 'across' and ferre 'to carry'. French carried it to English, where it began in law and spread to transport, money, and data.
intro.cn: transfer 是拉丁语 transferre“搬过去”，由 trans-“越过”加 ferre“搬运”构成。经法语进入英语，最早用于法律，后来扩展到交通、金钱与数据。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, bear, or bring. It is highly irregular and supplies the English family refer, offer, prefer, differ, suffer.
items.cn: ferre 意为搬运、承载、带来。它变化高度不规则，并衍生出英语的 refer、offer、prefer、differ、suffer。

items.en: Transferre meant to carry across, transport, or hand over. The prefix marks the boundary crossed; the verb marks the carrying.
items.cn: transferre 意为搬过去、运输、移交。前缀标记被越过的界线，动词标记搬运本身。

items.en: Ferre's past participle was suppletive: translatus, from which English gets translate and translation. Transfer and translate are twins of the same verb.
items.cn: ferre 的过去分词是异根形式 translatus，英语的 translate、translation 由此而来。transfer 与 translate 是同一动词的双胞胎。

items.en: Old French transferer meant to transfer property or rights. The legal sense was the first to reach English.
items.cn: 古法语 transferer 意为移转财产或权利。法律义是最早进入英语的义项。

items.en: English transfer appears in the 14c. in legal contexts: conveyance of property from one holder to another.
items.cn: 英语 transfer 于 14 世纪出现在法律语境中：财产从一方移转给另一方。

items.en: Railways added the change-of-vehicle sense, banks the money sense, and computing the data sense. All keep the same 'carry across' frame.
items.cn: 铁路增加了换乘义，银行增加了转账义，计算机增加了数据传输义。它们都保留同一个“搬过去”的框架。

note.en: The first group is transfer's legal and psychological family; the second separates moving, conveying, and shifting.
note.cn: 第一组是 transfer 的法律与心理词族；第二组区分移动、运送与转变。

entries.definition: able to be moved or conveyed to another holder or setting.
entries.definitionCN: 可转移的；可转让的；可迁移的。

entries.definition: the act of transferring, especially the redirecting of feelings onto a new person.
entries.definitionCN: 转移；尤指把情感转向新对象的移情。

entries.definition: the person who receives what is transferred.
entries.definitionCN: 受让人；被调动的一方。

entries.definition: the person who transfers something to another.
entries.definitionCN: 转让人；出让方。

entries.definition: to change place or position. It is the general word and does not require a receiving place.
entries.definitionCN: 改变位置。它最一般，不要求有一个接收方。

entries.definition: to move something slightly or to change direction. It is often a partial, not a complete, relocation.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微移动或改变方向。它常是部分而非整体迁移。

entries.definition: to carry something from one place to another, especially by a vehicle or channel. It stresses the carrying route.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一处运到另一处，尤通过车辆或渠道。它强调运输路线。

entries.definition: to move a business or person to a new location, usually permanently. It stresses the new base.
entries.definitionCN: 把企业或人迁到新地点，通常永久。它强调新的基地。

entries.definition: to give control or possession to someone else. It matches the legal and personal sides of transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 把控制权或占有交给别人。它对应 transfer 的法律义与人际义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin trans- 'across' + ferre 'carry', with the suppletive participle translatus. Family words transfer, transferable, transference, transferor, transferee.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 trans-“越过”+ ferre“搬运”，过去分词是异根形式 translatus。词族为 transfer、transferable、transference、transferor、transferee。

normal.en: Trans + ferre: carry across. Everything else is a different kind of load.
normal.cn: trans + ferre：搬过去。其余义项只是换了不同的“货物”。

normal.en: Transfer and translate are twins: both use the participle translatus.
normal.cn: transfer 与 translate 是双胞胎：两者都用分词 translatus。

normal.en: A transfer student is a person carried from one school to another.
normal.cn: 转学生，就是被从一所学校搬到另一所的人。

normal.en: Transfer money moves a claim; transfer a design moves a pattern; transfer a player moves a contract.
normal.cn: 转账移动的是请求权；转印移动的是图案；转会移动的是合同。

normal.en: At the platform you are both the luggage and the porter.
normal.cn: 在站台上，你既是行李，也是搬运工。

abstract.en: Transfer is the belief that what is valuable can survive a change of hands.
abstract.cn: 转移，是相信有价值的东西能在易手之后继续存在。

abstract.en: Some things lose nothing in transit; some lose everything.
abstract.cn: 有些东西在搬运中毫发无损，有些则失去一切。

abstract.en: A transfer is a small promise that the new holder will be as careful as the old.
abstract.cn: 转移是一个小小的承诺：新的持有者会像旧的持有者一样小心。

examples.en: The patient was transferred to a larger hospital overnight.
examples.cn: 病人连夜被转送到一家更大的医院。

examples.en: Ownership transfers only when the deed is registered.
examples.cn: 只有契据登记后，所有权才发生移转。

examples.en: He transferred his savings into a tax-free account.
examples.cn: 他把储蓄转入一个免税账户。

dict_mnemonic.text: “传思佛”——把思绪托给佛，从此处传到彼处 → transfer 转移、换乘

root: 源自拉丁语 transferre“搬过去”，由 trans-“越过”+ ferre“搬运”构成；核心是“把东西从这边搬到那边”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of transfer, all one carrying motion: an object, a person, money, a right, a traveller, a feeling, a player, or an image crosses from one holder or place to another.
sensesIntro.cn: transfer 的八个义项都是同一个搬运动作：物件、人、钱、权利、旅客、感情、球员或图像，从一边越过到另一边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box carried from one vehicle onto another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只箱子从一辆车被搬到另一辆车上。

branches.en: PHYSICAL CARGO: a file on a server and an image on clay are both loads carried across a surface.
branches.cn: 实物货物：服务器上的文件与陶土上的图像，都是被搬过某个表面的货物。

branches.en: PEOPLE: an employee moved to a new office and a player moved to a new club are the same institutional handover.
branches.cn: 人：调到新办公室的员工与转到新俱乐部的球员，是同一种制度性递交。

branches.en: CLAIMS: money and legal title are abstract loads whose ownership moves with the transfer.
branches.cn: 请求权：金钱与法律产权是抽象货物，其归属随转移而移动。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: the traveller crosses from one vehicle to another at the platform.
branches.cn: 旅程：旅客在站台上从一辆车跨到另一辆。

branches.en: INNER ATTACHMENT: affection and loyalty are treated as loads that can be moved to a new person or cause.
branches.cn: 内心依恋：感情与忠诚被当作可以搬到新人或新事业上的货物。

intro.en: Transfer's family is built on Latin ferre. Suffixes mark what can be moved, the act, and the two parties; compounds name fees and windows.
intro.cn: transfer 的词族建立在拉丁语 ferre 上。后缀标记“可被移动”、动作与双方；复合词标记费用与窗口。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are ferre 'to carry', transferre 'to carry across', and the suppletive participle translatus 'carried across'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 ferre“搬运”、transferre“搬过去”，以及异根过去分词 translatus“被搬过去的”。

items.meaning: able to be moved or conveyed to another holder
items.meaningCN: 可转移的；可转让的（-able 表示“可被”）
items.example: The ticket is not transferable to another person.
items.exampleCN: 这张票不可转让他人。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to be transferred
items.meaningCN: 可转移性；可转让性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: Skills have limited transferability across industries.
items.exampleCN: 技能跨行业的可迁移性有限。

items.meaning: the act of transferring, especially of feelings onto a new object
items.meaningCN: 转移；尤指情感移情（-ence 构成动作或状态名词）
items.example: The therapist noted transference toward the analyst.
items.exampleCN: 治疗师注意到对分析师产生的移情。

items.meaning: the party that transfers something to another
items.meaningCN: 转让人；出让方（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The transferor must sign the deed.
items.exampleCN: 转让人必须签署契据。

items.meaning: the party that receives what is transferred
items.meaningCN: 受让人；接收方（-ee 表示受动者）
items.example: The transferee takes on the lease obligations.
items.exampleCN: 受让人承担租约义务。

items.meaning: a charge paid for a transfer, especially of a player
items.meaningCN: 转会费；转让费
items.example: The club paid a record transfer fee.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部支付了创纪录的转会费。

items.meaning: the period when players may move between clubs
items.meaningCN: 转会窗口；允许球员转会的时期
items.example: The deal was completed before the window closed.
items.exampleCN: 交易在转会窗口关闭前完成。

items.meaning: a student who moves from one school to another
items.meaningCN: 转学生
items.example: Transfer students need help with the new timetable.
items.exampleCN: 转学生需要有人帮他们适应新课表。

items.meaning: the legal passing of property from one owner to another
items.meaningCN: 所有权移转；产权转让
items.example: Registration completes the transfer of ownership.
items.exampleCN: 登记完成所有权的移转。

items.meaning: a site where waste is moved from small trucks to larger ones
items.meaningCN: 转运站；垃圾由小车转到大车的场所
items.example: The transfer station compacts waste before it leaves.
items.exampleCN: 转运站在垃圾运出前将其压实。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry across, transport, hand over

definition_en: to change something completely in form, nature, or appearance, or to convert it into a different system or state
core_image: 一块陶土在手中被重新塑成另一个形状。
scene: The new railway transformed the sleepy town into a commuter suburb.
sceneCN: 这里 transform 是「彻底改变、改造」（第 2 个义项：改造地方或社会）；句意：新铁路把这个沉寂的小镇改造成了通勤郊区。场景要点：新建车站、旧屋与新公寓、通勤人群。

derivatives.zh: 有变革作用的；起改造作用的

senses.title: Change form or appearance completely
senses.titleCN: 彻底变形：外形整个换掉
senses.definition: to change something completely in form or appearance, often beyond easy recognition
senses.definitionCN: 彻底改变某物的形状或外观，常到难以辨认的程度
senses.example: The flood transformed the valley into a lake.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水把山谷变成了湖泊。
senses.why: Latin forma is shape. Transformare is to put a thing into a new shape, so the first sense is almost literal: the old form is replaced by another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 forma 是形状。transformare 就是把某物放进一个新形状，因此第一个义项几乎是字面：旧形被另一个形替换。

senses.title: Reform a place or system
senses.titleCN: 改造：把地方或制度重塑
senses.definition: to change a place, institution, or society radically for the better
senses.definitionCN: 彻底改变一个地方、机构或社会，使之变好
senses.example: The canal transformed the region's economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这条运河改变了该地区的经济。
senses.why: A region or an economy also has a shape: its arrangement of work, roads, and money. To transform it is to give that arrangement a new form.
senses.whyCN: 一个地区或经济也有形状：工作、道路与金钱的排列方式。改造它，就是给这种排列一个新形式。

senses.title: Convert data or a mathematical expression
senses.titleCN: 变换：把数据换成另一种表示
senses.definition: to convert data, a function, or an expression into a different representation without losing its information
senses.definitionCN: 把数据、函数或表达式转换为另一种表示而不丢失信息
senses.example: The Fourier transform turns a signal into its frequencies.
senses.exampleCN: 傅里叶变换把信号转换成它的频率成分。
senses.why: The thing keeps its identity but takes a new form. Mathematics uses transform for exactly this: same content, different shape, and the shape is reversible.
senses.whyCN: 事物保持同一性，但换了一个形式。数学用 transform 正是指此：内容相同、形状不同，而且可以逆回去。

senses.title: Change electrical voltage
senses.titleCN: 变压：把电压换成另一种水平
senses.definition: to change the voltage of an alternating current, as a transformer does
senses.definitionCN: 改变交流电的电压，如变压器所做
senses.example: The substation transforms 11,000 volts down to 240.
senses.exampleCN: 变电站把一万一千伏降到二百四十伏。
senses.why: Voltage is a level, and transforming it changes that level while the power continues. The form is the ratio; the energy is what passes through.
senses.whyCN: 电压是一种水平，变压就是改变这个水平而电力继续通过。形式是比值，能量才是穿过的东西。

senses.title: Change oneself or one's look
senses.titleCN: 变身：把自己改成另一个样子
senses.definition: to change one's own appearance, character, or life completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底改变自己的外貌、性格或生活
senses.example: She transformed herself for the role.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这个角色彻底改变了自己。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the shaping hand on the self. Clay that reshapes itself is still clay, but the form is new, and that is the point of the word.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把塑形的手转向自己。能重塑自己的陶土仍是陶土，但形式是新的，这正是这个词的要义。

senses.title: Convert a cell or organism
senses.titleCN: 转化：让细胞带上新性状
senses.definition: to introduce new genetic material into a cell so that its behaviour or traits change
senses.definitionCN: 把新的遗传物质导入细胞，使其行为或性状改变
senses.example: The researchers transformed the bacteria to produce insulin.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员转化这些细菌，使其生产胰岛素。
senses.why: Biology borrows the word for a lasting change of form and function inside a living cell. The new shape is chemical, but it is still forma.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借这个词指活细胞内部形态与功能的持久改变。新形状是化学层面的，但仍然是 forma。

senses.title: Convert a linguistic structure
senses.titleCN: 转换：语法里的形式改写
senses.definition: in linguistics, to derive one sentence structure from another by rule
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，按规则从一种句式派生出另一种
senses.example: The passive sentence is transformed from the active one.
senses.exampleCN: 被动句由主动句转换而来。
senses.why: Transformational grammar treats the deep structure as a shape and the surface sentence as another. The same information is re-formed by rule.
senses.whyCN: 转换生成语法把深层结构当作一种形状，把表层句子当作另一种。同样的信息按规则被重新塑形。

senses.title: Convert energy from one form to another
senses.titleCN: 能量转化：从一种形式变成另一种
senses.definition: to change energy from one form, such as chemical or kinetic, into another
senses.definitionCN: 把能量从化学能、动能等形式转换成另一种形式
senses.example: The engine transforms chemical energy into motion.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机把化学能转化为运动。
senses.why: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only re-formed. Transform is the precise verb for that, and it keeps the image of shape changing while substance stays.
senses.whyCN: 能量不能被创造或消灭，只能被重新塑形。transform 正是这一点的精确动词，它保留了“实质不变、形状改变”的意象。

intro.en: Transform is Latin transformare, from trans- 'across, beyond' and forma 'shape'. The word means to put something into a new form, and English has extended it from bodies to systems, data, and energy.
intro.cn: transform 是拉丁语 transformare，由 trans-“越过、超出”与 forma“形状”构成。词义是把某物放进新形式，英语把它从形体扩展到制度、数据与能量。

items.en: Forma meant shape, form, mould, and also beauty. It is the source of form, formal, format, and formula.
items.cn: forma 意为形状、形式、模子，也指美。它是 form、formal、format、formula 的来源。

items.en: Transformare meant to change the form of, to reshape, or to metamorphose. The prefix adds the idea of crossing into another state.
items.cn: transformare 意为改变形状、重新塑形、变形。前缀加入了“跨进另一种状态”的意思。

items.en: Transformatio was a change of form, used of physical shape and of rhetorical rearrangement.
items.cn: transformatio 指形式变化，用于物理形状，也用于修辞上的重组。

items.en: Old French transformer carried the word into English with the sense of changing appearance or nature.
items.cn: 古法语 transformer 把这个词带进英语，义为改变外观或性质。

items.en: English transform first meant to change one's form or to be changed, often in religious and literary writing.
items.cn: 英语 transform 最早指改变自身形式或被改变，常见于宗教与文学写作。

items.en: Science added the technical senses: voltage transformation, energy conversion, data transforms, and biological transformation.
items.cn: 科学增加了技术义：电压变换、能量转换、数据变换与生物转化。

note.en: The first group is transform's own family; the second separates change, convert, alter, and reshape by how deep the change goes.
note.cn: 第一组是 transform 自身的词族；第二组按“改变有多深”区分 change、convert、alter、reshape。

entries.definition: a complete change of form or nature.
entries.definitionCN: 形式或性质的彻底改变；转变、改造。

entries.definition: a device that changes voltage, or a person who brings about change.
entries.definitionCN: 变压器；带来变革的人。

entries.definition: having the power to change something deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 有深层变革作用的。

entries.definition: relating to transformation, especially in grammar or leadership.
entries.definitionCN: 转换的；变革性的，尤用于语法或领导力。

entries.definition: to become or make different. It is the widest word and says nothing about depth.
entries.definitionCN: 变得或使变得不同。它范围最广，不说明改变的深度。

entries.definition: to change something into a different form or use, often deliberately. It stresses the new function.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物改成另一种形式或用途，常带目的性。它强调新功能。

entries.definition: to change something in part, leaving much of it intact. It is weaker than transform.
entries.definitionCN: 部分改变，大部分保留。它比 transform 弱。

entries.definition: to give a new shape or structure. It is close to transform and often used of organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 赋予新形状或结构。它接近 transform，常用于组织。

entries.definition: to change something so completely that the old order no longer holds. It is the strongest of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底改变，使旧秩序不再成立。它是这组词中最强的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin trans- 'across, beyond' + forma 'shape' gives transformare 'reshape'. Family words transform, transformation, transformer, transformative, transformational.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 trans-“越过、超出”+ forma“形状”构成 transformare“重塑”。词族为 transform、transformation、transformer、transformative、transformational。

normal.en: Trans + forma: cross into a new shape.
normal.cn: trans + forma：跨进一个新形状。

normal.en: Format and formula share forma; transform is the shape that moves.
normal.cn: format 与 formula 共享 forma；transform 是那个会移动的形状。

normal.en: A transformer does not make new power; it re-forms the same power at another voltage.
normal.cn: 变压器不制造新电力，只是把同样的电力重新塑造成另一个电压。

normal.en: Data keeps its information but changes its form: that is a transform.
normal.cn: 数据保留信息却改变形式，这就是一次变换。

normal.en: Transformational grammar re-forms a deep sentence into a surface one.
normal.cn: 转换语法把深层句子重新塑造成表层句子。

abstract.en: Nothing is destroyed in a true transformation; the shape is what changes.
abstract.cn: 真正的转变不毁灭任何东西，改变的只是形状。

abstract.en: We transform places by changing what they are for, not only how they look.
abstract.cn: 我们改造一个地方，靠改变它的用途，而不只是它的外观。

abstract.en: To be transformed is to survive as the same thing in a form you did not choose.
abstract.cn: 被转变，就是以同一个东西的身份，活在你未曾选择的形式里。

examples.en: The discovery transformed our understanding of the immune system.
examples.cn: 这一发现彻底改变了我们对免疫系统的理解。

examples.en: The old warehouse was transformed into a gallery.
examples.cn: 旧仓库被改造成了一座画廊。

examples.en: Photosynthesis transforms light into chemical energy.
examples.cn: 光合作用把光转化为化学能。

dict_mnemonic.text: “穿石佛”——穿石成佛，形态整个变了 → transform 转变、改造

root: 源自拉丁语 transformare“重塑”，由 trans-“越过、超出”+ forma“形状”构成；核心是“把旧形状换成新形状”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of transform, all one reshaping: appearance, a place, data, voltage, the self, a cell, a sentence, or energy keeps its substance while taking a new form.
sensesIntro.cn: transform 的八个义项都是一次重塑：外观、地方、数据、电压、自我、细胞、句子或能量，实质保留而形式更新。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clay pressed into a new shape by two hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：陶土在双手中被重新压成另一个形状。

branches.en: OUTWARD FORM: an object and a person can both be given a new appearance while remaining themselves.
branches.cn: 外形：物体与人被赋予新外观，同时仍是自身。

branches.en: SYSTEMIC CHANGE: a place or society is reshaped in its arrangement, not merely in its surface.
branches.cn: 系统改变：地方或社会在结构上被重塑，而不只是表面。

branches.en: FORMAL CONVERSION: data and sentences change representation while keeping their information.
branches.cn: 形式转换：数据与句子改变表示方式，同时保留信息。

branches.en: ENERGY: voltage and energy change level or form, which is re-shaping at the level of physics.
branches.cn: 能量：电压与能量改变水平或形式，是物理层面的重塑。

branches.en: LIVING CHANGE: a transformed cell carries a new instruction that alters what it does.
branches.cn: 生命改变：被转化的细胞携带新指令，改变了它的行为。

intro.en: Transform's family is built on Latin forma. Suffixes mark the act, the agent, and the quality; technical compounds name mathematical and industrial transforms.
intro.cn: transform 的词族建立在拉丁语 forma 上。后缀标记动作、施动者与性质；技术复合词标记数学与工业变换。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are forma 'shape', transformare 'reshape', and transformatio 'a change of form'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 forma“形状”、transformare“重塑”，以及 transformatio“形式改变”。

items.meaning: a complete change of form or nature
items.meaningCN: 转变；彻底改变（-ation 构成动作名词）
items.example: The transformation of the docks took twenty years.
items.exampleCN: 码头的改造花了二十年。

items.meaning: having the power to produce deep change
items.meaningCN: 有变革作用的；能带来深层改变的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: The trip was a transformative experience.
items.exampleCN: 这次旅行是一次带来蜕变的经历。

items.meaning: a device that changes voltage, or a person who changes things
items.meaningCN: 变压器；变革者（-er 表示装置或人）
items.example: A transformer hummed on the pole outside.
items.exampleCN: 外面的电线杆上一台变压器嗡嗡作响。

items.meaning: changed completely in form
items.meaningCN: 被彻底改变的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The transformed district attracts new residents.
items.exampleCN: 改造后的城区吸引了新居民。

items.meaning: causing change, or undergoing change
items.meaningCN: 正在改变（事物）的（-ing 构成分词与形容词）
items.example: Transforming growth factor is a signalling protein.
items.exampleCN: 转化生长因子是一种信号蛋白。

items.meaning: relating to transformation, especially in grammar or leadership
items.meaningCN: 转换的；变革性的，尤用于语法或领导力（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Transformational grammar was influential in the 1960s.
items.exampleCN: 转换生成语法在 1960 年代影响很大。

items.meaning: to change so as to become something else
items.meaningCN: 转变成（into 标记结果形态）
items.example: The caterpillar transforms into a butterfly.
items.exampleCN: 毛毛虫变成蝴蝶。

items.meaning: to change starting from an earlier state
items.meaningCN: 从……转变而来（from 标记原状态）
items.example: The site transformed from a quarry into a park.
items.exampleCN: 该地从采石场变成了公园。

items.meaning: the reorganisation of an organization around digital technology
items.meaningCN: 数字化转型；围绕数字技术重组组织
items.example: The bank invested heavily in digital transformation.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行在数字化转型上投入巨大。

items.meaning: a mathematical operation that converts a signal into its frequency components
items.meaningCN: 傅里叶变换；把信号转换为频率成分的数学运算
items.example: The Fourier transform reveals hidden periodicities.
items.exampleCN: 傅里叶变换揭示隐藏的周期性。

latinEntries.meaning: to change the form of, reshape

definition_en: the process or period of changing from one state, system, or stage to another
core_image: 一座架在两种状态之间的窄桥，走过去就换了岸。
scene: The transition from coal to gas cut emissions sharply.
sceneCN: 这里 transition 是「转变、过渡」（第 1 个义项：从一种状态过渡到另一种）；句意：从煤到天然气的转变大幅降低了排放。场景要点：老煤炉与新燃气管道、跨越的桥、下降的排放曲线。

collocations.phrase: the transition from A to B
collocations.zh: 从 A 到 B 的过渡

senses.title: A change from one state to another
senses.titleCN: 转变：从这一岸走到那一岸
senses.definition: the process of changing from one state, condition, or system to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种状态、状况或制度变为另一种的过程
senses.example: The transition from school to work is often difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 从学校到工作的转变常常很艰难。
senses.why: Latin transire is trans- 'across' plus ire 'go'. A transition is a going across, so the word pictures movement between two banks rather than a thing changing in place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 transire 是 trans-“越过”加 ire“走”。transition 就是一次“走过去”，因此这个词画的是两岸之间的移动，而不是原地变形。

senses.title: The period of change
senses.titleCN: 过渡期：走在桥上的那段时间
senses.definition: the period during which a change is taking place, especially between two settled states
senses.definitionCN: 变化正在发生的时期，尤指两个稳定状态之间的阶段
senses.example: The country is in transition after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，这个国家处于过渡期。
senses.why: The crossing takes time. When the emphasis falls on duration, transition names the interval on the bridge rather than the arrival on the far bank.
senses.whyCN: 过桥需要时间。当重点落在持续时间上，transition 指桥上的那段时间，而不是到达对岸。

senses.title: A linking passage in writing
senses.titleCN: 过渡：段落之间的小桥
senses.definition: a sentence, phrase, or paragraph that connects one idea or section to the next
senses.definitionCN: 连接一个观点或段落与下一部分的句子、短语或段落
senses.example: The essay needs a transition between these two paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在这两段之间需要一个过渡。
senses.why: A text is also a series of banks. A transition sentence is the narrow bridge that lets the reader cross without falling into the gap.
senses.whyCN: 文本也是一连串河岸。过渡句就是那座窄桥，让读者跨过去而不掉进缝隙。

senses.title: A personal change of gender role
senses.titleCN: 性别过渡：从一种身份走到另一种
senses.definition: the process by which a person changes their gender presentation or social role
senses.definitionCN: 个人改变性别表现或社会角色的过程
senses.example: She began her transition in her thirties.
senses.exampleCN: 她在三十多岁时开始了性别过渡。
senses.why: The word's neutral 'crossing' fits a change that is social and personal at once. It names the process rather than any single step, which is why it is preferred.
senses.whyCN: 这个词中性的“跨越”义，恰好适合同时涉及社会与个人的改变。它命名的是过程而非某一步，因此被优先使用。

senses.title: A change of physical phase
senses.titleCN: 相变：物质跨过那条界线
senses.definition: in physics, a change between states of matter such as solid, liquid, and gas
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中物质在固、液、气等状态之间的变化
senses.example: The phase transition occurs at zero degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 相变发生在零度。
senses.why: Ice to water is a crossing at a fixed point. Physics borrowed the word because the substance stays the same while its state goes across a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 冰变水是在固定点上的跨越。物理学借这个词，因为物质本身不变，而它的状态跨过了一条界线。

senses.title: A musical change of key or section
senses.titleCN: 转调：音乐走过一个关口
senses.definition: a passage in music that moves from one key, theme, or section to another
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中从一个调、主题或段落转向另一个的过渡段
senses.example: The symphony's transition to the minor key is sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 这部交响曲转向小调的过渡很突然。
senses.why: Music marks time as a path, and a key change is a gate on that path. The transition is the bars that carry the listener through the gate.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把时间标记成一条路，转调就是路上的一个关口。过渡段就是把听众带过这个关口的那几小节。

senses.title: A switch between attack and defence
senses.titleCN: 攻防转换：球场上的换岸
senses.definition: in sport, the moment a team changes from defence to attack or the reverse
senses.definitionCN: 体育中球队由守转攻或由攻转守的那一刻
senses.example: Their transition play is the best in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的攻防转换是联赛中最出色的。
senses.why: A game flips between two states many times. The transition is the instant of crossing, and teams train to make that instant faster.
senses.whyCN: 比赛在两种状态之间反复翻转。transition 就是跨越的那一瞬，球队训练正是为了让这一瞬更快。

senses.title: To undergo or cause a change (rare verb)
senses.titleCN: 转变（罕用动词）：走过去
senses.definition: to make or undergo a transition; a rare verb use mostly found in technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 使转变或经历过渡；罕用动词，多见于技术写作
senses.example: The system transitioned to the new protocol overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 系统在一夜之间切换到新协议。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb keeps the same crossing. Modern usage allows it especially in computing and organizational change, though many style guides still prefer the noun.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词后仍是同一次跨越。现代用法尤其在计算机与组织变革中允许这样用，不过许多文体指南仍偏好名词。

intro.en: Transition is Latin transitio 'a going across', from transire 'to go across', built on trans- 'across' and ire 'to go'. French brought it to English, where it named both physical passage and rhetorical bridge.
intro.cn: transition 是拉丁语 transitio“走过去”，来自 transire“越过”，由 trans-“越过”与 ire“走”构成。法语把它带进英语，既指物理通过，也指修辞上的过渡。

items.en: Ire meant to go. It is irregular and appears in ambition, initial, circuit, and exit, all words about going.
items.cn: ire 意为“走”。它变化不规则，出现在 ambition、initial、circuit、exit 等与“行走”有关的词中。

items.en: Transire meant to go across, pass over, or pass away. It could describe a river, a border, or the end of a life.
items.cn: transire 意为越过、通过、逝去。它可以描述河流、边境，也可以描述生命的结束。

items.en: Transitio was the noun of action: a crossing, a passage, and in rhetoric a transition between topics.
items.cn: transitio 是动作名词：跨越、通过；在修辞学中指话题之间的过渡。

items.en: French transition carried both the physical and rhetorical senses into English in the 16c.
items.cn: 法语 transition 于 16 世纪把物理义与修辞义一起带进英语。

items.en: Political and industrial writing made the word central for changes of regime and economy. The 'period of change' sense grew from there.
items.cn: 政治与工业写作让这个词成为政权与经济变化的中心词。“过渡期”义由此生长。

items.en: The 20c. added phase transitions in physics, gender transition, and sports transition. All are crossings between two states.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了物理相变、性别过渡与体育攻防转换。它们都是在两种状态之间的跨越。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin going root; the second compares words for change by whether they name a process, a passage, or a result.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语“走”词根；第二组按“命名过程、通道还是结果”比较各种变化词。

entries.definition: the act of passing through or carrying goods through a place. It is the journey, not the change of state.
entries.definitionCN: 通过或运送货物经过某地。它指行程，而不是状态改变。

entries.definition: belonging to a period of change.
entries.definitionCN: 过渡期的；过渡性质的。

entries.definition: of the nature of a transition; a rarer variant.
entries.definitionCN: 具有过渡性质的；较少用的变体。

entries.definition: of a verb, taking a direct object. It shares the 'passing across' root but is a grammatical term.
entries.definitionCN: 指动词带直接宾语。它共享“传递过去”的词根，但属于语法术语。

entries.definition: the act or fact of becoming different. It is the widest word and need not imply two stable states.
entries.definitionCN: 变得不同这一行为或事实。它范围最广，不必然意味着两个稳定状态。

entries.definition: a small or gradual change, especially in position, emphasis, or direction. It is less structural than transition.
entries.definitionCN: 位置、重点或方向上的小幅或渐变。它不如 transition 那样结构性。

entries.definition: the act of moving through or from one place to another. It keeps the physical crossing without the state change.
entries.definitionCN: 通过或从一处到另一处的行为。它保留物理跨越，但不含状态改变。

entries.definition: the process of changing something into a different form or use. It stresses the result, not the journey.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物改为另一种形式或用途。它强调结果，而不是过程。

entries.definition: a change from one system or method to another, especially an abrupt one. It names the switch itself.
entries.definitionCN: 从一种制度或方法转为另一种，尤指突然的转换。它命名转换点本身。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin trans- 'across' + ire 'go' gives transire 'go across', and transitio 'a crossing'. Family words transition, transitional, transit, transitive.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 trans-“越过”+ ire“走”构成 transire“走过去”，再构成 transitio“跨越”。词族为 transition、transitional、transit、transitive。

normal.en: Trans + ire: go across. A transition is a crossing.
normal.cn: trans + ire：走过去。transition 就是一次跨越。

normal.en: Transit is the journey; transition is the change of bank.
normal.cn: transit 是行程；transition 是换岸。

normal.en: A transition sentence is a bridge a reader can walk on.
normal.cn: 过渡句是读者能走的一座桥。

normal.en: Ice to water is a phase transition: the same substance crosses a line.
normal.cn: 冰变水是相变：同一物质跨过一条线。

normal.en: A fast team trains the instant of crossing, not just the two banks.
normal.cn: 快节奏的球队训练的是跨越的那一瞬，而不只是两岸。

abstract.en: Every transition asks us to live for a while on a bridge with no ground under it.
abstract.cn: 每次过渡，都要求我们在没有地面的桥上住一阵。

abstract.en: The hardest part of change is not leaving one bank but trusting the other.
abstract.cn: 改变最难的部分，不是离开这一岸，而是相信那一岸。

abstract.en: A transition is only complete when the far bank becomes ordinary.
abstract.cn: 只有对岸变得平常，过渡才算完成。

examples.en: The transition to renewable power will take decades.
examples.cn: 向可再生能源的过渡将需要数十年。

examples.en: Students are given a week of transition activities before the new term.
examples.cn: 新学期开始前，学生有一周的过渡活动。

examples.en: The film uses a slow transition between the two scenes.
examples.cn: 影片在两个场景之间用了缓慢的过渡。

dict_mnemonic.text: “穿椅子”——从这把椅子穿到那把椅子，换了个位置 → transition 过渡、转变

root: 源自拉丁语 transire“越过、走过去”（trans-“越过”+ ire“走”），名词 transitio“跨越”；核心是“从这一岸走到那一岸的桥”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of transition, all one crossing: between states, between periods, between paragraphs, between genders, between phases, keys, or sides of a pitch.
sensesIntro.cn: transition 的八个义项都是一次跨越：状态之间、时期之间、段落之间、性别之间、物相之间、调性之间，或球场的攻守之间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow bridge between two banks, with no ground in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：架在两岸之间的窄桥，中间没有地面。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PERIOD: the crossing itself, and the time spent on the bridge.
branches.cn: 过程与时期：跨越本身，以及在桥上度过的时间。

branches.en: TEXT: a written transition is a bridge built between two paragraphs.
branches.cn: 文本：书面过渡是两段之间搭起的一座桥。

branches.en: IDENTITY AND MATTER: a person's social crossing and a substance's change of phase share the same boundary image.
branches.cn: 身份与物质：人的社会跨越与物质的相变，共享同一个边界意象。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE: music and sport both mark the instant of crossing and train it.
branches.cn: 表演：音乐与体育都标记跨越的一瞬，并加以训练。

branches.en: VERB USE: the rare verb turns the bridge into an action someone performs.
branches.cn: 动词用法：罕用的动词把桥变成某人执行的动作。

intro.en: Transition's family is built on Latin ire 'go'. Suffixes mark the adjective and the act; compounds name periods, metals, and sentences.
intro.cn: transition 的词族建立在拉丁语 ire“走”上。后缀构成形容词与动作名词；复合词标记时期、金属与句子。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are ire 'to go', transire 'to go across', and transitio 'a crossing'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 ire“走”、transire“走过去”，以及 transitio“跨越”。

items.meaning: relating to or belonging to a period of change
items.meaningCN: 过渡的；过渡期的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: A transitional government took office.
items.exampleCN: 一个过渡政府上台执政。

items.meaning: in a transitional manner
items.meaningCN: 以过渡方式地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The rules applied transitionally for one year.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则作为过渡适用了一年。

items.meaning: of the nature of a transition; rarer
items.meaningCN: 过渡性质的（较少用，-ary 构成形容词）
items.example: A transitionary clause was added to the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 条约中加入了一项过渡条款。

items.meaning: the act of passing through, or to pass through
items.meaningCN: 通过；过境；穿越（名词与动词）
items.example: The goods were damaged in transit.
items.exampleCN: 货物在运输途中受损。

items.meaning: of a verb, taking a direct object
items.meaningCN: 及物的；带直接宾语的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Break is transitive in break the glass.
items.exampleCN: 在 break the glass 中，break 是及物的。

items.meaning: the time allowed for a change to take place
items.meaningCN: 过渡期；允许变化发生的时间
items.example: The transition period ends in June.
items.exampleCN: 过渡期在六月结束。

items.meaning: a metal whose atoms have partly filled inner electron shells
items.meaningCN: 过渡金属；内层电子未填满的金属
items.example: Iron and copper are transition metals.
items.exampleCN: 铁和铜都是过渡金属。

items.meaning: a change between solid, liquid, gas, or other phases
items.meaningCN: 相变；固、液、气等相之间的变化
items.example: Melting is a phase transition.
items.exampleCN: 融化是一种相变。

items.meaning: currently in the middle of a change
items.meaningCN: 处于过渡中；正在转变
items.example: The industry is in transition.
items.exampleCN: 该行业正处于过渡之中。

items.meaning: a sentence that connects one section to the next
items.meaningCN: 过渡句；连接前后段落的一句
items.example: Add a transition sentence before the second example.
items.exampleCN: 在第二个例子前加一个过渡句。

definition_zh: 传送；传播；传染；传导；发射
definition_en: to send a signal, message, disease, trait, or force from one place or person to another
core_image: 一只手把一封密封的信递给下一个人，一路不停。
scene: Mosquitoes transmit the disease during the rainy season.
sceneCN: 这里 transmit 是「传播（疾病）」（第 2 个义项：把疾病传给他人）；句意：蚊子在雨季传播这种疾病。场景要点：蚊帐、显微镜下的病原体、雨季水洼、预防告示。

pos.zh: 传送；传播；传染；传导；发射

senses.title: Send a signal or data
senses.titleCN: 传输：把信号送过去
senses.definition: to send electronic signals, data, or information from one device or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把电子信号、数据或信息从一个设备或地点送到另一个
senses.example: The station transmits data every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 该站每十分钟传输一次数据。
senses.why: Latin transmittere is trans- 'across' plus mittere 'send'. A signal is a letter sent across a distance, so data transmission is the oldest image made invisible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 transmittere 是 trans-“越过”加 mittere“送”。信号就是跨越距离送出的一封信，因此数据传输是把最古老的意象变得看不见。

senses.title: Spread a disease
senses.titleCN: 传播疾病：把病原送给人
senses.definition: to pass a disease from one person, animal, or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把疾病从一个人、动物或地点传给另一个
senses.example: Ticks transmit Lyme disease to humans.
senses.exampleCN: 蜱虫把莱姆病传播给人类。
senses.why: The sender is a mosquito or tick and the message is a pathogen. The word treats infection as something carried across a boundary into a new body.
senses.whyCN: 发送者是蚊子或蜱虫，信息是病原体。这个词把感染当作被送过边界、进入新身体的东西。

senses.title: Pass on knowledge or culture
senses.titleCN: 传递文化：把知识送向后代
senses.definition: to pass on knowledge, stories, customs, or culture from one generation or group to another
senses.definitionCN: 把知识、故事、习俗或文化从一代人或群体传到另一代
senses.example: The songs transmitted the history of the tribe orally.
senses.exampleCN: 这些歌以口头方式传递了部落的历史。
senses.why: A message can be a whole culture. Here the sending is across time rather than space, but the letter is still handed on intact.
senses.whyCN: 信息可以是一整套文化。这里送出的是跨越时间而非空间，但那封信仍被完整地递下去。

senses.title: Pass a gene or trait to offspring
senses.titleCN: 遗传：把性状送进下一代
senses.definition: to pass a gene or inherited trait from parent to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 把基因或遗传性状从亲代传给子代
senses.example: The mutation is transmitted through the mother's line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个突变通过母系遗传。
senses.why: Genes are messages written in chemistry. Transmission here is a sending that no one can refuse, from body to body across generations.
senses.whyCN: 基因是用化学写成的信息。这里的传播是一种无人能拒绝的送出，跨越世代，从身体到身体。

senses.title: Broadcast by radio or television
senses.titleCN: 发射：把节目送到空中
senses.definition: to send out radio or television signals carrying programmes
senses.definitionCN: 发送承载节目的无线电或电视信号
senses.example: The station transmits on two frequencies.
senses.exampleCN: 该台用两个频率发射。
senses.why: Broadcasting is one sender and many receivers. The word keeps the one-way send of a letter but multiplies the recipients to everyone in range.
senses.whyCN: 广播是一个发送者、许多接收者。这个词保留了一封信的单向送出，却把收件人扩展到范围内所有人。

senses.title: Conduct heat, light, or sound
senses.titleCN: 传导：让能量穿过介质
senses.definition: of a material or medium, to allow heat, light, sound, or force to pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 指材料或介质让热、光、声或力穿过
senses.example: Water transmits sound better than air.
senses.exampleCN: 水传声比空气好。
senses.why: The medium does not create the energy; it carries it across. This is the passive side of the same verb, where the letter passes through a channel.
senses.whyCN: 介质不创造能量，只把它送过去。这是同一个动词的被动一面：信穿过一条通道。

senses.title: Send a document formally
senses.titleCN: 转送：把文件正式送到
senses.definition: to send a document, report, or payment to a person or office, especially formally
senses.definitionCN: 把文件、报告或款项送到某人或某机构，尤指正式地
senses.example: Please transmit the signed copy to our legal office.
senses.exampleCN: 请把签署后的副本转送我们的法务办公室。
senses.why: This is the literal letter again. Formal correspondence uses transmit when the act of sending is itself official and must be recorded.
senses.whyCN: 这里又回到字面的信。正式函件用 transmit，是因为“送出”这一动作本身具有官方性质，必须记录在案。

senses.title: Pass property to heirs
senses.titleCN: 传让：把财产交到继承人手里
senses.definition: in law, to transfer property or rights to heirs or successors
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产或权利传给继承人或承继者
senses.example: The estate was transmitted to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产被传给长子。
senses.why: The legal sense is transmission across generations by rule. The letter is property, and the sending is fixed by law rather than by choice.
senses.whyCN: 法律义是按规则跨代传递。信是财产，而送出由法律而非个人意愿决定。

intro.en: Transmit is Latin transmittere, from trans- 'across' and mittere 'to send'. French transmitted the word to English, and its senses run from letters and disease to radio and genes.
intro.cn: transmit 是拉丁语 transmittere，由 trans-“越过”与 mittere“送”构成。法语把词带入英语，义项从信件、疾病一路走到无线电与基因。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, let go, or release. It underlies admit, submit, permit, mission, and missile.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走、释放。它支撑着 admit、submit、permit、mission、missile。

items.en: Transmittere meant to send across, transfer, or pass on. The prefix marks the far side; the verb marks the sending.
items.cn: transmittere 意为送过去、移交、传递。前缀标记那一头，动词标记送出。

items.en: The past participle transmissus meant sent across. English transmission comes from the corresponding noun transmissio.
items.cn: 过去分词 transmissus 意为“被送过去的”。英语 transmission 来自对应的名词 transmissio。

items.en: Old French transmettre carried the word into English, first in legal and administrative contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 transmettre 把词带进英语，最早用于法律与行政语境。

items.en: English transmit first meant to convey property or send a message. The medical sense of passing disease appears later.
items.cn: 英语 transmit 最早指移转财产或送出消息。“传播疾病”的医学义出现较晚。

items.en: Radio and telegraphy made the broadcast sense central in the 19c., and genetics and computing added their own transmissions.
items.cn: 19 世纪无线电与电报让“发射”义成为中心，遗传学与计算机又各自增加了自己的 transmission。

note.en: The first group is transmit's own family; the second separates sending, spreading, and conducting by what travels and through what.
note.cn: 第一组是 transmit 自身的词族；第二组按“什么在 travel、通过什么”区分送、播、导。

entries.definition: the act of sending or spreading, and the gears that carry power in a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 传送或传播的行为；也指车辆中传递动力的变速器。

entries.definition: a device that sends signals, or a person or organism that passes something on.
entries.definitionCN: 发射机；传递者；传播病原的生物。

entries.definition: able to be sent or spread from one to another.
entries.definitionCN: 可传送的；可传播的。

entries.definition: the act of sending documents or a letter that accompanies them.
entries.definitionCN: 文件转送；随文件附上的转送函。

entries.definition: to cause something to go to a destination. It is the plain word and makes no claim about the channel.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物去到目的地。它最普通，不说明渠道。

entries.definition: to carry or communicate something. It stresses the carrying of a message or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 运送或传达。它强调消息或情感的承载。

entries.definition: to send signals or programmes to many receivers at once. It is transmit with a widened audience.
entries.definitionCN: 向许多接收者同时发送信号或节目。它是受众扩大的 transmit。

entries.definition: to extend over a larger area or among more people. It stresses diffusion rather than a directed send.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展到更大范围或更多人之中。它强调扩散，而非定向送出。

entries.definition: to give something to the next person. It matches the cultural and genetic senses.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物交给下一个人。它对应文化传递与遗传义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin trans- 'across' + mittere 'send' gives transmittere 'send across'. Family words transmit, transmission, transmitter, transmittable, transmittal.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 trans-“越过”+ mittere“送”构成 transmittere“送过去”。词族为 transmit、transmission、transmitter、transmittable、transmittal。

normal.en: Trans + mittere: send across. A letter, a signal, a germ, a gene.
normal.cn: trans + mittere：送过去。可以是信、信号、病菌或基因。

normal.en: Mission and transmit share mittere: both are about sending.
normal.cn: mission 与 transmit 共享 mittere：两者都与“送”有关。

normal.en: A mosquito is a transmitter with wings.
normal.cn: 蚊子就是一台长了翅膀的发射机。

normal.en: Water transmits sound because it carries the wave without making it.
normal.cn: 水能传声，因为它承载波而不制造波。

normal.en: A car's transmission sends engine power to the wheels.
normal.cn: 汽车的 transmission 把发动机的动力送到车轮。

abstract.en: To transmit is to trust a channel you cannot see.
abstract.cn: 传输，就是信任一条你看不见的通道。

abstract.en: Some messages arrive intact; some arrive changed by the medium.
abstract.cn: 有些信息完好抵达，有些被介质改变。

abstract.en: Nothing spreads by itself; something always carries it.
abstract.cn: 没有东西会自己传播，总得有什么在携带它。

examples.en: The antenna transmits a weak signal across the valley.
examples.cn: 天线把一个微弱信号传过山谷。

examples.en: The trait is transmitted only when both parents carry the gene.
examples.cn: 只有父母双方都携带该基因时，这个性状才会遗传。

examples.en: Please transmit the report before Friday's deadline.
examples.cn: 请在周五截止前转送报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: “传丝密特”——把丝密密码传过去 → transmit 传送、传播

root: 源自拉丁语 transmittere“送过去”（trans-“越过”+ mittere“送”）；核心是“把东西送过一段距离交到下一处”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of transmit, all one sending: a signal, a disease, a culture, a gene, a broadcast, a sound wave, a document, or an inheritance crosses from sender to receiver.
sensesIntro.cn: transmit 的八个义项都是一次送出：信号、疾病、文化、基因、广播、声波、文件或遗产，从发送者越到接收者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter handed from one person to the next, never stopping.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封密封的信从一个人递到下一个人，从不停下。

branches.en: SENDING: data, a broadcast, and a formal document are all messages sent to a receiver.
branches.cn: 送出：数据、广播与正式文件，都是送往接收者的消息。

branches.en: BODIES: disease and genes are carried into new bodies, one by contact and one by inheritance.
branches.cn: 身体：疾病与基因被送进新身体，一个靠接触，一个靠遗传。

branches.en: CULTURE: stories and customs are letters sent across time.
branches.cn: 文化：故事与习俗是跨越时间送出的信。

branches.en: MEDIUM: a channel carries energy across without creating it.
branches.cn: 介质：通道把能量送过去，却不创造能量。

branches.en: LAW: property is transmitted to heirs by rule, the sending fixed in advance.
branches.cn: 法律：财产按规则传给继承人，送出方式是预先固定的。

intro.en: Transmit's family is built on Latin mittere. Suffixes mark the act, the agent, the possibility, and the formal document; compounds name lines and diseases.
intro.cn: transmit 的词族建立在拉丁语 mittere 上。后缀标记动作、施动者、可能性与正式文件；复合词标记线路与疾病。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are mittere 'to send', transmittere 'to send across', and transmissio 'a sending across'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 mittere“送”、transmittere“送过去”，以及 transmissio“送过去的行为”。

items.meaning: the act of sending or spreading; also a vehicle's gear system
items.meaningCN: 传送；传播；变速器（-sion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Transmission of the virus occurs by contact.
items.exampleCN: 病毒通过接触传播。

items.meaning: a device that sends signals, or an organism that passes something on
items.meaningCN: 发射机；传播者（-er 表示装置或施动者）
items.example: The transmitter was mounted on the roof.
items.exampleCN: 发射机安装在屋顶上。

items.meaning: able to be sent or spread
items.meaningCN: 可传送的；可传播的（-able 表示“可被”）
items.example: The infection is transmittable before symptoms appear.
items.exampleCN: 这种感染在症状出现前就可传播。

items.meaning: the act of sending documents, or a covering letter
items.meaningCN: 文件转送；转送函（-al 构成动作名词）
items.example: A transmittal letter accompanied the drawings.
items.exampleCN: 图纸附有一封转送函。

items.meaning: sending or spreading; in operation as a sender
items.meaningCN: 正在传送的；作为发送端运行的（-ing 构成分词）
items.example: The transmitting tower is 300 metres tall.
items.exampleCN: 这座发射塔高三百米。

items.meaning: to send a signal or message on again
items.meaningCN: 转发；重新发射（re- 表示再次）
items.example: The satellite retransmits the data to the ground station.
items.exampleCN: 卫星把数据转发给地面站。

items.meaning: to send something to a receiver
items.meaningCN: 把某物传送给（to 标记接收者）
items.example: The results were transmitted to the ministry.
items.exampleCN: 结果被传送给该部。

items.meaning: to pass something along a medium
items.meaningCN: 通过某介质传送（through 标记介质）
items.example: Light is transmitted through the thin film.
items.exampleCN: 光透过这层薄膜。

items.meaning: passed from one person to another through sexual contact
items.meaningCN: 性传播的；通过性接触传给他人
items.example: The clinic tests for sexually transmitted infections.
items.exampleCN: 该诊所检测性传播感染。

items.meaning: the cable or system that carries electrical power or signals
items.meaningCN: 输电线路；传输线
items.example: The storm damaged the transmission line.
items.exampleCN: 风暴损坏了输电线路。

latinEntries.meaning: to send across, transfer, pass on

definition_en: the general direction in which something is changing, a fashion, or to move or develop in a particular direction
core_image: 一条在地图上缓缓拐弯的线：不是某个点，而是往哪边走。
scene: The trend in rainfall has been downward for twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 trend 是「（数据的）走势」（第 3 个义项：数据随时间变化的方向）；句意：二十年来降雨量呈下降趋势。场景要点：折线图、向下的箭头、雨量计、年份刻度。

senses.title: The general direction of change
senses.titleCN: 总趋势：事情往哪边走
senses.definition: the general direction in which a situation, condition, or process is developing
senses.definitionCN: 情况、条件或过程发展的总体方向
senses.example: There is a trend towards smaller families.
senses.exampleCN: 出现了家庭规模变小的趋势。
senses.why: The Old English verb trendan meant to turn. A trend is the direction in which things have been turning, so it names a course rather than a single event.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 trendan 意为“转”。trend 就是事物一直在转向的那个方向，因此它命名的是一条走向，而不是单个事件。

senses.title: A fashion or vogue
senses.titleCN: 潮流：众人跟着转向
senses.definition: a widespread fashion or style, especially in clothes, design, or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 广泛流行的风尚或风格，尤指服装、设计或行为方面
senses.example: The trend for wide trousers returned last year.
senses.exampleCN: 阔腿裤的潮流去年又回来了。
senses.why: Many people turning the same way at the same time is a fashion. The word keeps the idea of a shared direction, but the direction is now set by taste.
senses.whyCN: 许多人同时转向同一个方向，就是风尚。这个词保留了“共同方向”的意思，只是方向现在由品味决定。

senses.title: A statistical tendency over time
senses.titleCN: 走势：数据线上的斜率
senses.definition: a persistent tendency in data over time, which may rise, fall, or stay level
senses.definitionCN: 数据随时间持续呈现的倾向，可上升、下降或持平
senses.example: The trend in rainfall has been downward for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年来降雨量呈下降趋势。
senses.why: Statistics draws the turning as a line on a graph. The trend is the slope of that line, which is why the word is so often used with up and down.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把这种转向画成图上的线。trend 就是那条线的斜率，因此这个词常与 up、down 连用。

senses.title: The drift of opinion or events
senses.titleCN: 动向：舆论往哪边偏
senses.definition: the general drift of public opinion, policy, or events, often observed rather than planned
senses.definitionCN: 公众意见、政策或事件的总体倾向，常是被观察到的而非被计划的
senses.example: The trend of the debate favoured the reformers.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论的动向有利于改革派。
senses.why: Opinion also turns. When many small judgements lean the same way, the direction becomes visible as a trend, even though no one designed it.
senses.whyCN: 意见也会转。当许多小判断都朝同一边偏，方向就以 trend 的形式显现，尽管没有人设计它。

senses.title: To move in a particular direction (verb)
senses.titleCN: 呈趋势：价格往那边走
senses.definition: to change or develop in a particular direction over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间朝某一方向变化或发展
senses.example: Prices have trended upward since the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 自春天以来价格呈上升趋势。
senses.why: The noun became a verb without changing its image. To trend upward is simply to be turning that way, observed over a span rather than at a point.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词，意象未变。trend upward 就是一直在往那边转，是在一段时间里观察到的，而不是某一刻。

senses.title: To turn (archaic verb sense)
senses.titleCN: 转向：这个词最老的动作
senses.definition: the older sense of to turn, bend, or take a direction, still found in dialect and historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 较古的“转、弯、取向”义，仍见于方言与历史写作
senses.example: The road trends north after the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥，路转向北方。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense of trendan: to turn. The modern noun is that turning seen as a path, so the oldest layer explains all the others.
senses.whyCN: 这是 trendan 最原始的身体动作义：转。现代名词就是把这次转向看作一条路径，因此最古老的一层解释了其余义项。

senses.title: The direction of a geographical feature
senses.titleCN: 走向：山谷延伸的方向
senses.definition: the general line or direction in which a valley, ridge, or coastline extends
